title: HAYDUKE BASE Canopy - Lite Versatility
description:
https://squirrel.ws/parachutes/base-jumping/hayduke

HAYDUKE is an ultralite & low-bulk parachute that represents what we think is an ideal balance of performance and passive safety. HAYDUKE offers improved glide, yet retains the benefit of slow forward speed in DBS. The result: more time for object avoidance in the case of an off-heading, with agile handling that allows for fast, easy, and efficient (low sink rate) turns using risers or brakes.

ULTRALITE PN9 with ZP leading edge
FLOAT FLAPS at rear-chord
Expanded SLAT System at center span
5 Vents & Advanced Crossports for rapid inflation
Staggered Brake Cascade
Low-freefall to terminal performance

title: AURA 3
description:
What factors are critical in a performance WS BASE design? 
Start Arc, for margin on exit. 
Glide performance, for reaching objectives. 
Speed range, to reduce the tendency of stall. 
Stable and usable speed, for increased maneuverability. 
Flare power, for safe and immediate separation from terrain, and margin for deployment. 
The AURA 3 was designed from the ground up by veteran WS BASE jumpers with these points in mind.

title: Simon Fasnacht - Jungfrau
description: “Doing a jump from the Jungfrau always means a lot to me. This exit was opened by Patrick Kerber on the 11th of August 2013. He was my wingman for many years. Coming here is always a tribute to him for all of the effort he put into wingsuit BASE jumping. After about 16 years of wingsuit BASE jumping I am extremely happy to be living in Switzerland with the opportunity to jump every day. The Wengener Jungfrau jump is a true classic. It not only requires good piloting, but also mountain skills. Jumping with rope and crampons is not something you do every day. So we recommend to do the needed training, before. Also, light is right, in the case of this flight you want to be carrying the minimum of equipment. Also, it is season specific. Get the right beta to have the right timing and setup. The Wengener Jungfrau usually is jumped in August to late September when temperatures and winds in high altitude are nice and calm. Enjoy the POV and when you do it next time, pay your respects to our friend Patrick who planned and jumped it in a different time…”

title: ZAK
description:
Zak Tessier is one of the most dedicated, committed, experienced, and skilled wingsuit BASE jumpers that we have ever met... and this is how Zak flies his Squirrel AURA.  http://squirrel.ws
Zak Tessier is a bit of an odd duck - if you have hung out much in Lodi, CA, or Lauterbrunnen, Switzerland, then you’ve probably met him - living out of a van, living to jump – and you probably sensed his intense dedication to our sport, and for pushing himself to a higher level each day. His raw, frothy passion for BASE is almost freakish, and can make a normally passionate jumper feel somewhat lame and part-time by comparison.
If you’re seeing him for the first time in this whacky video, then there are a couple of things you need to know: First, Zak has built these tricks on a foundation of fifteen years of freeflying experience and 8,681 skydives. He has 1,568 BASE jumps and just this year alone he has completed almost 800 BASE jumps in the US and Europe, the vast majority of them being wingsuit BASE jumps in the Alps. He is at a level of practice, currency, and dedication that very few people on planet earth have ever achieved in wingsuit BASE jumping.

You will use a BASE parachute (in the skydive environment) to learn advanced canopy skills that are critical to object avoidance and safe landings in BASE. You will learn to pack a BASE rig, go through advanced water training, learn the basics of BASE rigging, and more. title: JEB CORLISS Chooses SQRL BASE JUMPING EQUIPMENT
description:
Our friend Jeb Corliss chooses SQRL wingsuits & BASE gear. 
In almost 25 years of BASE jumping, Jeb Corliss has done some of the gnarliest things that this sport has ever seen. If you entered the sport of BASE in the past 10 years or so, you might not know this. And no one cares less about impressing you than Jeb, so it falls to us to explain: In the early 2000s, before social media, before youtube, back when we recorded our jumps on actual videotape, Jeb was nailing handstand exits to double gainers from low and positive slider down cliffs. When many of today’s jumpers were in elementary school, he was throwing twisting quads from sub-terminal cliffs and was a wingsuit BASE pioneer. By the time facebook was invented, Jeb already had over 1000 BASE jumps on multiple continents and was one of the most prolific jumpers in history. He turned his exploits into an actual BASE career, survived horrific accidents, and is still going strong. 
 
Putting a legendary BASE career aside, what is most impressive about Jeb is that he is one of the realest, most honest jumpers we have known. He gives zero fucks about what anyone thinks, especially other jumpers, but at the same time he is nice to everyone and is a genuinely kind person. His motivation to jump is, and always has been, pure. He has faced the inevitability of his own death honestly and sincerely, and he jumps only for himself. That he has turned it into a job with made-for-TV stunts is simply a manifestation of his drive to BASE jump more. 
               
After years of jumping SQRL wingsuits, Jeb has chosen to switch to SQAD BASE gear as well. In his words: “I’ve been skydiving since 1994 and BASE jumping since 1997. When it comes to gear, I can jump whatever I like. I’ve been jumping Squirrel wingsuits for many years now and have been amazed at their customer service, quality of craftsmanship, and research & development. I decided it was time to demo their BASE gear and over the last 6 months I have really put it through its paces. I was impressed with the quality they’ve been able to achieve. I‘m getting back into jumping in a serious way and now have some of the most serious gear available to help make that happen. Thank you Squirrel,  I’m excited for the upcoming season and can’t wait for the world to open up again so I can put this gear to good use.”

title: Proper Pin Tension for BASE Containers
description:
GAUGING PIN TENSION FOR WINGSUIT & TRACKING
Top pin tension: with both pins seated, and the pin cover flap open, you should be able to gently move your container around on the floor by pulling on the bridle just below the top pin, without the pin releasing. 

If you can pick your container up without the pin releasing, pin tension is too high. 

If you can’t move the rig around at all before the pin releases, pin tension is too low.  

This guide to pin tension is obviously very subjective. Ideal pin tension will vary with: 
Type of jump (slider down, slider up, wingsuit, tracking)
Airspeed at deployment 
Also note that how the harness/container is worn on the jumper (cinched very tight, or worn loosely, worn over more clothing or equipment) will affect pin tension. A tighter rig or a more hunched-over body position may increase pin tension when worn.
